slides.title:
Copilot Cost
Optimization Playbook
slides.subtitle: A hands-on, three-tier guide for engineering teams on Copilot Business, Enterprise, and Pro — built around the June 2026 shift to token-based AI Credits.

content.html:
In June 2026 the billing model
changed.

content.title: Before · Premium Requests
content: A fixed quota - say 300 requests/month. Each frontier-model call ate a multiple of one. Your typed prompt was the unit.

content.title: After · GitHub AI Credits
content: 1 credit = $0.01. Billed on the tokens you actually consume - input, output, and cached - at each model's published rate.

content.html: Why it matters: tokens come overwhelmingly from things you don't type — files attached as context, history re-sent every turn, tool schemas, and every autonomous agent step. One careless agent run can burn more credits than a hundred thoughtful chat messages.
Three levers control the cost of any interaction.

content.title: ① Which Model
content: Cheapest to most expensive is a ~20× spread on input tokens. Auto routes intelligently so you don't pay frontier prices for trivial work.

content.title: ② How Much Context
content: Your prompt is usually the smallest part. Attached files, conversation history, and tool schemas ride along on every turn.

content.title: ③ How Many Round-trips
content: One chat reply vs. forty agent steps. Every step is another metered model call.

content.html: Understand where tokens go and you can cut spend by half or more without losing capability. Every technique in this playbook pulls one of these three levers.
Not all models cost the same.
Auto mode reserves expensive reasoning models for genuinely hard problems and gives paid plans a 10% discount on model costs. Set it and leave it.
Habits everyone should adopt today.
They cost nothing to implement, require no admin rights, and deliver the biggest immediate savings. Do only this tier and you're already ahead of most organizations.

content.label: FREE
content.title: Use Completions
content: Inline ghost text and Next Edit Suggestions are unlimited and free on every paid plan. Don't open chat to write a five-line function.

content.title: Default to Auto
content: Smart routing + 10% discount for zero effort. The laziest way to save money is to not override it.

content.title: Be Specific
content: State the goal, the constraints, and when to stop. A vague prompt that produces a wrong answer costs you twice.

content.html: Let ghost text write routine code — $0.
The most underused fact about Copilot: inline completions never touch your credit pool. If you're filling in a function body or an obvious pattern, let the suggestions do it.

content.title: Do this

content: def calculate_invoice_total(items):
Start typing and let ghost text complete the body - free of charge.

content.title: Not this
content: Opening Copilot Chat and typing “write me a function that totals invoice line items” - a metered model call for something completions handle for free.

content.html: Output tokens cost roughly 5× the input.

content.title: Ask for Terse Output
content: Keep these in your back pocket:

items: "Code only, no explanation."
"Answer in one or two sentences."
"Just the diff."
"List the file names, don't show contents."

content.title: Fresh Chat per Task
content: A session re-sends its entire accumulated history on every turn. Your tenth question drags the previous nine back through the model as input. New task = new chat - reset the running context to zero.

content.html: Don't switch models mid-conversation without a reason. It breaks prompt caching and increases cost without much quality gain.
Match the mode to the task.

cells.value: Edits one or a few named files
A clear change to specific files
Autonomous loop: plans, reads, edits, runs tools

content.html: The mistake that quietly drains pools: reaching for Agent mode out of habit for a task that Ask or Edit would handle. Every step it takes is another metered call — and it can take dozens.
The basic tier in one screen.

items: Let inline completions write routine code — free
Model picker set to Auto
Prompts are specific: goal + constraints + stop condition
Ask for terse output when you don't need prose
New task = new chat
Ask < Edit < Agent — pick the smallest mode that works

content.html: Configuration that makes the cheap path the default path.
This tier moves from individual habits to configured behavior — settings, repository instructions, and context discipline for the whole team. Stop relying on willpower; start relying on setup.

content.title: Scope Context with #-refs
content: Tell Copilot exactly what to look at instead of letting it over-attach:
#file:checkout/totals.py #sym:apply_discount
Close unrelated editor tabs - open tabs are a silent context source.

content.title: Repository Instructions
content: A short .github/copilot-instructions.md is read on nearly every interaction. It eliminates the back-and-forth where Copilot guesses your conventions wrong. Keep it short - it loads every time.

content.html: Load instructions only where they apply.
For larger repos, attach instructions to specific paths so you don't pay for backend rules while editing frontend code. Use the applyTo frontmatter under .github/instructions/.

content.title: frontend.instructions.md

content: applyTo: "web/**/*.{ts,tsx}"
React 19 function components and hooks only. Tailwind utilities, no inline styles. Fetch via the useApi() wrapper.

items: "Don't refactor unrelated code" — cuts output tokens
"Don't add comments that restate the code"
"Don't add dependencies without flagging first"

content.html: Ship these guardrails in settings.json

items: summarizeAgentConversationHistory = true — auto-compacts long agent conversations so later turns don't drag the whole history
chat.agent.maxRequests = 15 — hard cap on model requests per agent run (default 25)
chat.utilityModel = gpt-5-mini — route commit messages, chat titles, and intent detection to a cheaper model
chat.tools.compressOutput.enabled = true — compresses large terminal output before sending

content.html: maxRequests is the standout: it converts an unbounded worst case ("the agent looped 60 times") into a bounded one. If the agent hits the cap, you decide to spend more — instead of discovering it after the fact.
You can't manage what you can't see.

content.title: Status Bar Dashboard
content: Click the Copilot icon in the VS Code Status Bar to see the percentage of your monthly AI-credit allowance used and your reset date. Glance at it like a fuel gauge.

content.title: Chat Debug View
content: Power users open ⋯ → Show Chat Debug View for per-interaction token counts - eye-opening the first time you watch one agent step consume thousands of tokens.

content.html: Awareness alone changes behavior. Make checking usage a habit before it becomes a surprise on the invoice.
Research → Plan → Implement
The highest-leverage intermediate practice. Instead of one long session that accumulates context, split complex work into three deliberate sessions — each starting with minimal, relevant context.

content.title: Research
items: Fresh chat, cheap model, Ask mode
"Explore how auth works. Don't edit."
You get a map of the key files and flow

content.title: Plan
items: Fresh chat — paste the summary
"Write a step-by-step plan. No code yet."
Review the approach while it's cheap to fix

content.title: Implement
items: Fresh chat, Agent mode
Paste the approved plan
"Implement step 1 only," then step 2…

content.html: Skills, hooks, MCP, and admin controls.
For power users, tech leads, and admins — the surfaces that can save the most and, left unmanaged, cost the most.

items: /context — visualize window usage
/compact — drop earlier exploration
/clear or /new — reset between tasks
/model gpt-5-mini — cheaper routine work

content.title: CLI Caveats
content: It auto-compacts at ~80%, but by then you've paid for a bloated context many times - compact proactively. Use Plan Mode (Shift+Tab) before big changes. Use /fleet sparingly: each subagent carries its own context window.

content.html: MCP servers are a silent token tax.
Each enabled tool injects its schema (~100–500 tokens) into the system prompt on every agent step — before the agent does anything useful.

The discipline: enable only what the current task needs. Treat MCP servers like browser extensions — keep them off by default in mcp.json and toggle on per-task via Configure Tools. Leaner tool sets are cheaper and more reliable.
Build lean, reusable automation.

items: Pin a cheap model (gpt-5-mini)
Minimal tool set - no edit tools for a reviewer
Cap output: "max 8 bullets, one line each"
"LGTM and nothing else" makes the common case nearly free
Run linters and type-checkers after each edit
Deterministic checks are free
Every bug a hook catches = a round-trip saved
Block destructive terminal commands with a human in the loop

content.html: The principle: push correctness onto free, deterministic tooling and reserve paid model reasoning for the genuinely ambiguous parts.
The four budget layers.

cells.value: The only hard per-person stop; a $0 ULB blocks a user immediately
Caps metered charges after the pool is exhausted
Tracks / limits spend for that org
Caps total metered charges after the pool

content.html: "Stop usage when budget limit is reached" is OFF by default. Left off, limits are alerts, not caps. And a $0 enterprise budget does not stop individual users — use universal ULBs as your real per-person control.
Monitor, alert, tune.

content.title: Dashboards
content: Use the AI usage dashboard and downloadable reports. Pooled credits mean light users subsidize heavy ones - look at the distribution, not just the total.

content.title: Alerts
content: Configure budget alerts at 75 / 90 / 100% and confirm who receives them before rollout.

content.title: Monthly Tuning
content: Blocked early? ULB too tight. Pool exhausting mid-cycle? Investigate agent/model patterns before raising the budget.

content.html: Promo window Jun–Sep 2026: Business gets ~3,000 credits/user and Enterprise ~7,000. Use it to capture your true baseline before the standard smaller pool returns.
The whole guide, compressed.

content.label: FREE
content.title: Routine Code
content: Inline completions. Ghost text. Don't open chat.

content.title: Quick Question
content: Ask mode + Auto. Terse output. One fresh chat.

content.title: Clear File Change
content: Edit mode + Auto. Use #file: to scope context.

content.title: Complex Feature
content: Research → Plan → Implement. Agent mode, maxRequests capped, only the MCP tools this task needs.

content.label: OF THE SAVINGS FROM THREE RULES

content.title: ① Smallest Mode
content: Completions are free; agent mode is expensive. Use the smallest mode that works.

content.title: ② Auto by Default
content: 10% off and smart routing for zero effort. Don't override it.

content.title: ③ Small Context
content: Scope with #refs, close tabs, start fresh sessions. Tokens you don't send are tokens you don't pay for.

content.html: Value per credit, not minimal usage.
The goal is not minimal usage — a team afraid to use Copilot is wasting the seats you bought. The goal is the most real engineering done for each dollar of tokens.

Spend freely on the hard problems where a frontier model in agent mode genuinely earns its cost. Be frugal on the routine work where a free completion or a cheap model does the same job. Cost discipline isn't a tax on productivity — it's what lets you afford the powerful tools exactly where they matter most.
